Question: The perimeter of an equilateral triangle exceeds the perimeter of a square by \(1989\) cm. The length of each side of the triangle exceeds the length of each side of the square by \(d\) cm. The square has perimeter greater than \(0.\) How many positive integers are not possible values for \(d?\)
